subject: Request: accelerate delivery of per-account throughput reservation for Aurora Systems
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Sanders <matthew.sanders@aurorasys.com>, pri yom.das@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Request: accelerate delivery of per-account throughput reservation for Aurora Systems

Matt — thanks again for the productive demo last week. Aurora's procurement team surfaced a commercial gating item: they need a contractual guarantee around minimum sustained throughput for their tenant during large batch workloads and an ability to burst above that baseline without noisy neighbor effects.

They've asked if we can ship a per-account throughput reservation and per-route burst bucket that: 
- guarantees a baseline RPS/token throughput for an account (configurable per SOW)
- preserves low tail latency for burst traffic by isolating burst capacity (soft reservation + fallback to shared pool)
- exposes per-route observability so they can audit quota consumption for compliance

Attachment: Aurora_requirements_summary.pdf (summary of ask from their architect).

This is a deal blocker for a $1.2M ARR commitment in Q4 if we can commit to a delivery window (customer target: production by 2027-01-15). Can product+eng evaluate scope & minimal viable implementation this week? If we can get a rough dev estimate and rollout plan I can lock the SOW and procurement will move.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, pri yom.das@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: accelerate delivery of per-account throughput reservation for Aurora Systems

Thanks Ben — looping in product/infra context.

Quick take: the feature set breaks down into three deliverables with different risk profiles:
1) Control-plane plumbing: per-account reservation objects + UI/API to configure baseline RPS and burst window. Low risk.
2) Runtime enforcement: scheduler/autoscaler changes to reserve a small dedicated pool and quota accounting to prevent noisy neighbors. Medium risk (requires changes across routing and autoscaler).
3) Observability: per-route token usage + alerts + export to Aurora's SIEM. Low-medium risk depending on retention & schema requirements.

Questions we need answered to scope properly:
- Acceptance criteria: what exact RPS baseline and burst headroom are they contracting for? (Ben, can you confirm numbers from procurement?)
- Will Aurora accept a soft-reserve with documented fallback (shared pool) during extreme load? Hard real-time reservations add much more complexity.
- Are they expecting cross-region failover guarantees?

From a product perspective we could ship a v1 (control-plane + soft-reserve + basic observability) as a configurable feature flag and then iterate on stronger enforcement in v2. Need engineering estimate to validate Jan 15 target.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior PM, Platform
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: accelerate delivery of per-account throughput reservation for Aurora Systems

Adding CS context — Aurora will only sign the SOW if the baseline is contractually explicit. Procurement asked for: 
- 100 RPS sustained at 1k token average payload per account as a baseline, with the ability to burst to 400 RPS for short periods (up to 10 minutes)
- SLA clause for P99 latency under baseline: <250ms
- Audit logs showing per-route consumption for last 90 days

They are willing to accept a soft-reserve (documented) for the burst fallback as long as there is an agreed escalation path and measurable telemetry. The $1.2M ARR commit is contingent on production by Jan 15, 2027 and a one-quarter penalty/credit clause if delivery slips more than 4 weeks.

I can surface exact procurement language (they shared a redline template) — attaching SOW draft. Attachment: Aurora_SOW_draft.docx

Priyom
Priyom Das
Customer Success Manager
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: accelerate delivery of per-account throughput reservation for Aurora Systems

Thanks for the clear asks. Engineering estimate and constraints below (rough):
- Minimal viable approach (v1 soft-reserve):
  * Control plane: add Reservation object (API + UI) + datastore changes — 2 engineer-weeks
  * Router/autoscaler: quota accounting + bias routing to reserved pool (soft enforcement) — 3 engineer-weeks
  * Observability: per-route counters surfaced to metrics + 90-day export job — 1 engineer-week
  * Testing/e2e and canary rollout + smoke infra changes — 1 engineer-week
  => Total: ~7 engineer-weeks (can be done with 3 engineers in ~3 calendar weeks if we permit overtime and unblock cross-team PRs).

- Risks/unknowns: cross-region failover and strict P99 enforcement under malicious load are non-trivial and push us to v2 (would require admission control and heavier runtime isolation).
- Delivery dependencies: prioritization on the infra backlog, CI capacity, and a staging canary environment. We will also need CS acceptance tests (Priyom to define).

If Sales can commit to the Jan 15 date as a hard customer expectation (and share the SOW redline), we can try to carve out a fast-path. Recommend: approve a light-guardrails scope (v1) with a follow-up v2 roadmap.

Karthik
Director, Serving Infrastructure
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: accelerate delivery of per-account throughput reservation for Aurora Systems

Appreciate the quick triage and realistic estimates. Confirming next steps: 
- Priyom will share the SOW redline by EOD tomorrow (11/13).
- Product (Olga) to scope v1 acceptance criteria based on the procurement numbers above and prepare a short PRD (1-pager) that we can use internally to greenlight prioritization.
- Eng (Karthik) to provision tentative resource commitment: 3 engineers (full time) for the fast-path and target Jan 15 prod with the caveat that any additional scope (hard reservations, cross-region guarantees) moves timeline.
- Sales will put the SOW into a conditional approval status and request procurement to remove the penalty clause for a v1 delivery acceptance test defined by CS.

I'll also add the HubSpot deal link to the Jira ticket. Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567
